articles.title: AlphaProof Code: How AI Agents Formally Verified Signal's Encryption in Four Weeks
articles.excerpt: AlphaProof Code: How AI Agents Formally Verified Signal's Encryption in Four Weeks Formal verification — mathematically proving that software does exactly what it claims — has long been the gold stand…
articles.body: AlphaProof Code: How AI Agents Formally Verified Signal's Encryption in Four Weeks Formal verification — mathematically proving that software does exactly what it claims — has long been the gold standard of software security. It is also notoriously expensive. Verifying the seL4 microkernel took twenty person-years. Verifying the CompCert C compiler took six. For most production software, that cost is simply out of reach. On November 10, 2026, Google DeepMind published AlphaProof Code , a multi-agent AI framework that completed a comparable feat in four weeks with a team of five researchers — and none of them wrote a single line of proof code. What Was Actually Verified The target was libsignal , the open-source reference implementation of the Signal protocol.

articles.title: Healthcare Appointment Ranking Signals: Retrieval Architecture for Semantic Search
articles.excerpt: Short answer: rank appointment content with a staged pipeline that applies hard clinical and time constraints first, then blends lexical, semantic, freshness, and provenance signals; keep the expensiv…
articles.body: Short answer: rank appointment content with a staged pipeline that applies hard clinical and time constraints first, then blends lexical, semantic, freshness, and provenance signals; keep the expensive index small enough to rebuild and every answer traceable to a source record. An appointment assistant is not a general question-answering bot. A result that is semantically close but for the wrong clinic, insurance plan, or date can create a harmful booking. In a payment ledger I would never let a fuzzy match decide which account moves money; scheduling deserves the same exactly-once mindset for intent and evidence. The index-cost constraint changes the design: retrieve a cheap, broad candidate set, then spend compute only on candidates that survive policy checks.

articles.title: Transactional Email Attachments — Template Ownership and Retention for Media Reports
articles.excerpt: The bill for emailing a generated media report has several possible components: message submission, attachment storage, retained message copies, and the engineering work needed to reconstruct a disput…
articles.body: The bill for emailing a generated media report has several possible components: message submission, attachment storage, retained message copies, and the engineering work needed to reconstruct a disputed send. For a concrete sizing example, take a 3 MiB PDF attachment. MIME base64 encoding turns its contents into 4 MiB before line wrapping and message headers. Retain ten independently stored encoded copies and that becomes 40 MiB of attachment payload. These are calculated sizes for an example, not measured traffic or a service quote. Short answer: choose a transactional email API by who owns the report template, which attachment representation crosses its boundary, and how long each copy survives.

articles.body: Lighthouse tells you how a page behaves on one machine, once. Your users get slower phones, worse networks and late third-party scripts. Core Web Vitals real user monitoring (RUM) closes that gap by measuring LCP, INP and CLS in the browsers of actual visitors and sending the data to a backend you control. This guide is about designing that system: the client collector, the payload, the ingestion endpoint, the data model, the aggregation queries and the alerting, with the trade-offs at each step. If you are looking for the optimization work itself (images, caching, scripts, fonts), start with our guide on how to improve website speed in 9 steps . This article is about knowing, with evidence, which fixes matter for your real traffic and whether a deploy made things worse.

Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally. According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again." Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week.

articles.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
articles.excerpt: Conspiracy theories surround the odd-looking appearance of a shadow seen in the final images captured by Phobos 2, the Soviet Union’s last mission into deep space.
articles.body: On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft.

articles.title: I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector showed me what I’m missing
articles.excerpt: This budget-priced projector reminded me what light pollution has taken from us
articles.body: I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it. Instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution . A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making plans for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images.

articles.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
articles.excerpt: Three stars, 28 light-years, and one big cosmic mystery.
articles.body: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour.
